context: Naoko receives a delivery and signs for it gruffly; chats with the deliveryman briefly.

lines.speaker: takeda_officer
lines.jp: お届けです、署名お願いします。
lines.en: I have a delivery for you — could you sign here, please?
lines.style: Warm, professional courtesy. Even-paced. Gentle knock on "sign." No rush in the voice. The practiced ease of someone who does this every day but means it.

lines.speaker: naoko_aunt
lines.jp: おう、おおきに、ご苦労さん。
lines.en: Yeah, thanks — appreciate the hard work.
lines.style: Brash Kansai greeting, bright and generous. Quick up-tempo opening. Genuine appreciation, not condescending. The voice of someone who feeds delivery people because they respect the work.

lines.speaker: takeda_officer
lines.en: I'll set the package down here for you.
lines.style: Gentle, unhurried. Small smile in the voice. Meticulous but not stiff — making space for the package like it matters. Soft landing on each word.

lines.speaker: naoko_aunt
lines.en: Yes, I've got it — thank you.
lines.style: Warm and satisfied. A small nod in the voice. Brisk but not dismissive — the closing warmth of someone pleased with the exchange and moving forward.

lines.speaker: takeda_officer
lines.en: Then I'll be on my way — thank you for your time.
lines.style: Polite close, small bow in the voice. Composed, respectful. Neither hurried nor lingering. The professional grace of knowing when an exchange is complete.
